minutes.headline: Select Board held a Complete Streets workshop with consultants; no budget votes, only routine warrants read.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a workshop with state-funded consultants on Lunenburg's Complete Streets policy, adopted in April 2017. Board members, staff and residents named problem spots for sidewalks, crosswalks and speeding, and discussed state funding limits and how the projects would be paid for. The meeting ended with warrants read, a thank-you from a board member, and next meeting dates.

public_comment.topic: A resident who lives on Highland Street said the police force is short-staffed and speed enforcement is limited, and asked that protection of persons and property be considered.
A resident described high speeds on Lancaster Avenue and asked for sidewalk extension toward the center of town.
Residents raised a damaged sidewalk from Turkey Hill Road toward Chestnut Street and Highland as the route to the baseball fields.

votes.motion: Warrants read: accounts payable, payroll and another warrant; vote called but result not in captions

budget_items.what_was_said: Approval of the policy made the town eligible for state technical assistance, used to hire the consultants.
Consultants said the town can apply for contributory funds for projects on the prioritization list.
A board member said Chapter 90 funds are woefully inadequate and wants to know what the town must contribute before projects are pursued.
Staff suggested tying small sidewalk and striping projects to roads already funded for paving.
Town pays for design; the cost spreadsheet will carry design and construction estimates. Striping adds to annual maintenance.
Accounts payable and payroll warrants were read.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent most of the meeting in a workshop with state-funded consultants on the town's Complete Streets policy; no budget votes were taken.
Consultants said the town can apply for state construction funds for projects on a prioritization list, and a board member questioned whether Chapter 90 funds are enough.
Residents named problem spots for sidewalks, crosswalks and speeding, including Lancaster Avenue, Highland Street and the route from Turkey Hill Road toward the ball fields.
Consultants will compile project lists, issue a public survey in the coming weeks, and draft a prioritization plan with design and construction cost estimates.
The board read the routine warrants; the vote result is not audible in the captions. The next meetings were noted for January 16 and January 23.

why_it_matters: Sidewalk and crosswalk projects that reach the prioritization list may qualify for state construction money, but the town pays for design and for yearly upkeep such as striping, which falls on the town budget, mostly taxes.
Staff suggested tying small projects to roads already funded for paving, so which streets get repaved may shape where sidewalk work happens.
